title: Idgham without ghunnah: merging into laam and raa: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 1: Al-Qadr, Al-'Alaq 1 to 12 and the noon sakinah rules
source: Written for quran/y3 lesson 13 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Idgham without ghunnah rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 13. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

head: With ghunnah: ي ن م و
Without ghunnah: ل ر
Not this
This
rows: yakun-n-n lahu: a hum before the laam
yakul-lahu: the noon becomes laam, no hum

keywords.def: merging the noon into the next letter

questions.q: Read «هُمَزَةٍۢ لُّمَزَةٍ» (104:1). Which rule, and how?
questions.a: Idgham without ghunnah: tanween merges into laam; read humazatil-lumazah with no hum.

questions.q: Sort on the pupil PDF: put eight examples into 'with ghunnah' and 'without ghunnah'. Today's rota group recites Al-'Alaq 96:1 to 4 to the teacher in turn.
questions.a: With: خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْ, لَهَبٍۢ وَتَبَّ, فَمَن يَعْمَلْ, مِّن مَّسَدٍ. Without: وَيْلٌۭ لِّكُلِّ, يَكُن لَّهُۥ, أَن رَّءَاهُ, عِيشَةٍۢ رَّاضِيَةٍۢ.

questions.q: Extend: find one idgham without ghunnah in Surat Al-Ikhlas.
Stretch: why do you think the hum disappears before laam and raa?
questions.a: Laam and raa are made very close to the noon and fully take its place, so no hum is left.

questions.q: «وَيْلٌۭ لِّكُلِّ» (104:1): how do we read the tanween?
options: Merge into laam with no hum
questions.a: A) Merge into laam with no hum. Laam is an idgham letter without ghunnah. Humming is for ي ن م و; clear is for throat letters.

questions.q: Think again: Some friends join so well you can't tell who is who. Before laam and raa the noon vanishes completely. What do you think we hear?
questions.a: Only the laam or raa, doubled, with no humming: idgham without ghunnah.
